input: The wall thickness of the compressor casing, once the corrosion allowance has been added, amounts to 44 mm, and the joint at the casing flange is closed using a gasket that has been selected on the basis of temperature limit alone. Of the two gasket materials that were considered, the higher-rated one is preferred, since the flange is exposed to the full discharge temperature at the metal face and the lower-rated material reaches its limit well within the normal operating range of the machine. In terms of pressure rating, the two materials are not separated: at the $\Delta P$ for which the joint has been designed, both materials are able to seal effectively, so the choice ultimately turns on the temperature margin that each material leaves available at the flange face. Similar reasoning also applies to the bolting check that follows the gasket choice, given that the load which the bolts are required to hold at temperature depends on the way in which the gasket relaxes, and a material that has been chosen for its temperature limit may nevertheless lose load more quickly than the joint can tolerate. Downstream of the compressor, the discharge line runs to the absorber, and the condensate collecting at the low point of this line is returned by the lean solvent pump; the duty of the pump is determined by the liquid rate, while its margin against cavitation is determined by the suction condition, which is expressed through NPSH at the pump inlet. One aspect that remains open at this stage is the interaction between the gasket choice and the flange facing, because a harder gasket with the higher temperature rating may require a facing finish that the existing flange does not currently have, and the facing finish specified for the current flange was originally selected for the softer material, which is where the comparison needs to be taken next.

A margin is needed because the face temperature is not steady: it follows the discharge through start-up, load changes and trips, and the excursions, not the steady running point, are what carry the face towards the limit of the weaker material. The two checks are kept apart in the design file, one for the pressure boundary and one for the suction condition.
